bibl.title: Reichsrecht and Volksrecht in Theory and Practice: Roman Justice in the Province of Egypt (P.Oxy. II 237, P.Oxy. IV 706, SB XII 10929).
bibl.seg: 145.4 P. Oxy. II, 237; IV, 706 P. Yale Inv. 1606
Anna Dolganov, Reichsrecht and Volksrecht in Theory and Practice: Roman Justice in the Province of Egypt (P.Oxy. II 237, P.Oxy. IV 706, SB XII 10929).
bibl.note: Offers a perspective on the traditional debate over the nature of the legal order in the Roman Empire, the role of Roman law in Roman provincial jurisdiction and the status of local laws and practices under Roman rule. These questions are explored through a series of case studies of papyrological evidence from Roman Egypt, including P. Yale Inv. 1606 (= S.B. XII, 10929), P. Oxy. II, 237 and P. Oxy. IV, 706. - Heraclides: a wronged patronus. - Chaeremon: a wronged paterfamilias. - Dionysia: a daughter victimized by her Egyptian father. - Conclusion.
